questions.text: S(x) = (7700 - 40x - x^2)/7700: find (a) the limiting age omega, (b) verify it's a valid survival function, (c) the survival function for a life aged 25, (d) the probability of death between 35 and 45 given aged 25, (e) the force of mortality at 50.
questions.originalText: Survival function S(x) = (7700−40x−x²)/7700: find (a) the limiting age ω, (b) verify it's a valid survival function, (c) ₂|q₀, (d) survival function for a life aged 25, (e) P(die between 35 and 45 | aged 25), (f) force of mortality at 50.

solution.hint: Find omega by setting S(omega)=0; the survival function for a life already aged 25 uses the conditional ratio S(25+t)/S(25).
solution.steps: **(a) Limiting age:** solve $7700-40\omega-\omega^2=0 \iff \omega^2+40\omega-7700=0$. By the quadratic formula, $\omega = \dfrac{-40+\sqrt{1600+30800}}{2}=\dfrac{-40+180}{2}=70$. **(b) Validity:** $S(0)=7700/7700=1$ \checkmark; $S$ is a downward-opening quadratic in $x$ restricted to $[0,70]$, and $S'(x)=(-40-2x)/7700<0$ throughout, so $S$ is strictly decreasing \checkmark; $S(70)=0$ \checkmark — all survival-function criteria hold on $[0,70]$. **(c/d) Survival function for a life aged 25:** $_tp_{25} = \dfrac{S(25+t)}{S(25)}$. Compute $S(25)=(7700-1000-625)/7700 = 6075/7700$. **(e) P(die 35–45 | aged 25):** this is $_{10}p_{25} - {}_{20}p_{25} = \dfrac{S(35)-S(45)}{S(25)}$. Compute $S(35)=(7700-1400-1225)/7700=5075/7700$, $S(45)=(7700-1800-2025)/7700=3875/7700$. So the probability is $\dfrac{5075-3875}{6075} = \dfrac{1200}{6075} \approx 0.1975$. **(f) Force of mortality at 50:** $\mu(x)=\dfrac{-S'(x)}{S(x)} = \dfrac{40+2x}{7700-40x-x^2}$; at $x=50$: $\mu(50)=\dfrac{40+100}{7700-2000-2500}=\dfrac{140}{3200}=0.04375$.
solution.examReady: Solve S(ω)=0 for the limiting age; check S(0)=1, S decreasing, S(ω)=0 for validity; use S(x+t)/S(x) for conditional survival; use -S'(x)/S(x) for the force of mortality.
solution.commonMistakes: Forgetting to divide by S(25) (not S(0)) when computing probabilities conditional on already being alive at 25 — a very common source of lost marks.

questions.text: A borrower has a Tk 60,00,000 loan at j_12=15% over 7 years, with an early-repayment penalty of 3 months' payments. After the 15th payment, a bank offers j_12=12%. Should he refinance?
questions.originalText: A borrower has a Tk 60,00,000 loan at j₁₂=15% over 7 years, with an early-repayment penalty of 3 months' payments. After the 15th payment, a bank offers j₁₂=12%. Should he refinance?

solution.hint: Follow the four-step method: original payment, outstanding balance via the prospective method, new payment on (balance + penalty), then compare.
solution.steps: Method (see the fully worked 18,000/4-year version on the Annuities topic page for the identical procedure): (1) original monthly payment $P = 6{,}000{,}000 / a_{\overline{84}|j}$ at $j=0.15/12=0.0125$; (2) outstanding balance after 15 payments, $B = P\cdot a_{\overline{69}|j}$ (69 payments remaining); (3) at the new rate $j'=0.12/12=0.01$, new payment $P' = (B+3P)/a_{\overline{69}|j'}$ (balance plus the 3-month penalty, re-amortized over the same 69 remaining months); (4) refinance is worthwhile exactly when $P'<P$.
solution.finalAnswer: Numerical comparison of P and P' is needed to give a definitive yes/no — the interest-rate drop (15% → 12%) makes refinancing likely favourable once the penalty is absorbed, but the exact comparison requires evaluating the annuity factors above.
solution.commonMistakes: Forgetting to add the 3-month penalty to the outstanding balance before recomputing the new payment — the penalty must be financed too if the borrower doesn't pay it out of pocket.

questions.text: Define the components of a mortality table and their relationships; find total deaths expected between ages 55-60 given 600 deaths between 55-56 and q_55=0.01001, q_56=0.01038, q_57=0.01081, q_58=0.01122, q_59=0.01172.
questions.originalText: Define the components of a mortality table and their relationships; write formulas for probabilities of survival and death. Find total deaths expected between ages 55–60 out of a group aged 55, given 600 deaths between 55–56 and q₅₅=0.01001, q₅₆=0.01038, q₅₇=0.01081, q₅₈=0.01122, q₅₉=0.01172.

solution.hint: First recover l_55 from the given death count and q_55, then propagate l_x forward using l_{x+1}=l_x(1-q_x).
solution.finalAnswer: Approximately 3,175 total deaths expected between ages 55 and 60 (figures rounded at each step; a spreadsheet-precision calculation would refine the final digits).
solution.examReady: Recover l_55 from the given death count, propagate l_x = l_{x-1}(1-q_{x-1}) year by year, then total deaths = l_55 - l_60.
solution.commonMistakes: Rounding l_x too aggressively at each intermediate step, which compounds into a noticeably different final answer — keep several decimal places through the recursion.
